clauseEvidenceInventory.requirement:
#### BLOCK-015 — Assigned tasks with due dates

*Tier:* Core

**Requirement.** A task item (`BLOCK-007`) can carry one assignee and a due date. Typing `@` inside a task assigns the member mentioned, and typing the documented public door or choosing from the date picker sets the due date, which renders in the reader's locale and shows as overdue once it passes. The assignee gets one inbox item when assigned (`NOTIF-001`), by email or push under their delivery settings (`NOTIF-005`, `NOTIF-006`), and one reminder on the due date (`NOTIF-004`). Reassigning notifies the new assignee once and the previous assignee not at all, and an assignee completing their own task notifies no one. Assigning a member who cannot read the page asks the assigner to share the page with them or cancel, and never notifies that member. Completion still records who and when. Tasks are read and changed through the API and MCP (`API-001`, `API-003`) under the same checks. A task item stays a block, and it still never appears in a database view. Protocol and representation details are in [wiki doors](docs/wiki-doors.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. a browser journey at 1440 and 390 types a task, assigns it with `@` and sets a due date with the documented public door.
2. The assignee gets exactly one inbox item and, after a Workers journey advances time, exactly one due-date reminder.
3. Reassigning notifies only the new assignee.
4. Assigning a member without access prompts the assigner to share and sends that member nothing.
5. The task shows as overdue after its due date.

#### COLLAB-001 — Live co-editing by default

*Tier:* Core

**Requirement.** Two or more members with `edit` access can type in the same page, and in the same block, at the same time. Their characters merge without conflict: there is no 409 and no last-write-wins for concurrent text, and `SAVE-003` conflicts remain only for structural edits that cannot merge, such as editing a block another member deleted, which offers restore. Every accepted operation is durable before it is acknowledged. A member's access is rechecked on every operation. Narrowing or revoking access closes that member's socket within 5 seconds, keeps their unsent text locally as an unsaved draft (`SAVE-004`), and never applies it. Reconnecting replays unacknowledged operations exactly once. Saved means committed (`SAVE-001`).

**Acceptance.**
1. a two-browser journey at 1440 and 390 in which two members type into one paragraph at the same time and both see the same final text within 1 second.
2. It also covers a dropped connection that reconnects with no lost or duplicated characters, and a grant revoked mid-typing that closes the editor within 5 seconds, keeps the draft unsaved and lists no revision for it.
3. A Workers journey sends interleaved operations to the collaboration route and reads back one revision history.

#### IMP-013 — Old Confluence links resolve in Slate

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-INPUT-001, BASE-INPUT-002, BASE-INPUT-003 · *Rules:* D-2

**Requirement.** Every Confluence import, by file (`IMP-003`) or by API (`IMP-007`), keeps a link map in Slate from each imported space, page, blog post, attachment and comment to its Slate record. The map is keyed by source site and source ID, and keeps every title a page or post has had as an alias. Slate recognizes these old URL forms, on an `atlassian.net/wiki` site and on a Server or Data Center base URL: - tiny links (the documented public door, the documented public door), decoded with Confluence's tiny-link encoding of the page ID; - page-ID URLs (the documented public door, its editor forms, and `viewpage.action?pageId=123`); - title URLs (the documented public door), matched against the page's current and earlier titles; - blog URLs (the documented public door and the documented public door); - space home URLs (the documented public door, the documented public door) and attachment downloads (the documented public door); - `focusedCommentId` parameters and heading fragments, which carry through to the comment thread and the heading anchor. Slate serves the map itself, so the buyer needs no host of its own: - **Resolver route.** the documented resolver is an authenticated Slate route. A signed-out visitor signs in first and then continues, and learns nothing about the map before sign-in. A mapped URL redirects to the record's permanent URL (`LINK-001`). A member without access gets `LINK-004`'s access-needed state there and learns nothing more, and a deleted record resolves to its tombstone (`LINK-002`). An unmapped URL shows a "Not migrated" page with an "Ask an owner" action. It names the source space key when the URL or the import records carry it, and never a title. - **Old hostname.** An owner who controls the old hostname, such as a Server or Data Center site or a Confluence Premium custom domain, can add it as a legacy hostname and point it at the deployment. Every old path on it then redirects to the resolver on Slate's own origin, keeping the fragment. - **Chat.** An owner can add the old Confluence hostname to the Slack, Teams and Nook apps' unfurl domains. A newly posted old URL then unfurls as its Slate record under `CHAT-002`'s access rule, with an "Open in Slate" action. - **Browser.** Members with the browser extension are sent from the old site to Slate (`CARD-002`). - **Map export.** An owner can download the map as CSV (old URL, Slate URL) to serve from any proxy they run. Later passes add to the map (`IMP-014`). Complete export and restore carry it (`PORT-001`, `PORT-002`), and only an Undo removes entries, for the records it removes. Every unmapped URL that reaches the resolver after cutover is counted in the cutover report (`IMP-007`) by source URL, with no member identity. Protocol and representation details are in [wiki doors](docs/wiki-doors.md).

1. the `IMP-007` fixture and an `IMP-003` CSV export of the same space each import a page, a renamed page, a blog post, an attachment and an inline comment.
2. A Workers journey then requests the documented resolver with: - the page's tiny link, its page-ID URL and its `viewpage.action` URL; - the renamed page's old the documented public door title URL; - the blog URL and the attachment download URL; - the comment's `focusedCommentId` URL.
3. Each redirects to its imported record.
4. A member without access to the page follows the redirect and gets the access-needed state with no title.
5. A signed-out request reaches sign-in and reveals nothing else.
6. A URL from a space that was not imported shows "Not migrated" with its space key.
7. A request to a configured legacy hostname for the tiny link redirects to the resolver on the main origin and sets no cookie.
8. With a chat provider fake at the network edge, a posted page-ID URL unfurls as the Slate page for a reader and as "Restricted Slate page" for a non-reader. The downloaded CSV lists every mapped URL, and after export and restore into an empty deployment the tiny link still resolves. Exceeding the lookup limit returns 429.

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-INPUT-001, BASE-INPUT-002, BASE-INPUT-003 · *Rules:* D-2

**Requirement.** A link in an imported body whose target lies outside that import is kept as a pending link. #### API-001 — Public REST API

*Tier:* Core

**Requirement.** A versioned public REST API covers pages, blocks, databases, records, comments, search, members, groups and files, described by a published OpenAPI document. It uses cursor pagination, operation keys (`SAVE-005`), declared rate limits and a stable error shape. Authentication is a personal access token or an OAuth 2.0 app with scopes (read or write, per container). Every call acts as exactly one member and passes the same checks as the UI (`SHARE-002`, `LIFE-002`, `SEARCH-005`). Tasks (`BLOCK-015`) are read and changed through it, with their assignee, due date and completion, under the same checks and notifications as the UI: assigning a member who cannot read the page is refused until it is shared, and completion records who and when. Personal-token custody follows RL-101: full members and owners only, no guest tokens, explicit container scopes bounded by current UI rights, once-issued secrets stored as hashes, a disclosed 90-day default and one-year maximum, immediate revocation, no hashes in archives and permanently inactive restored credentials. Undeclared privileged operations remain denied. Protocol and representation details are in [wiki doors](docs/wiki-doors.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. a contract suite generated from the OpenAPI document runs every operation over HTTP with a token for each of two members, asserting the schemas and that every access difference matches the UI's.
2. Expired, revoked and under-scoped tokens are refused.
3. The suite assigns, dates, reassigns and completes a task and finds the same refusals, notifications and completion record as the UI.
4. Issue a once-visible full-member token with finite container scopes; after revocation, expiry or restore it executes no request, and guest issuance is refused (RL-101).

It asks short comprehension questions, answers follow-ups with citations, and routes confusion ("this step no longer matches") to the page owner as a flag. Its data is verified pages readable by the new member and their questions. The member controls whether their progress is shared. Their manager sees only the progress they agree to share, and nothing is inferred about performance. Formal courses and certifications belong to [Beam](https://github.com/just-every/run-beam).

**Acceptance.**
1. a browser journey assigns a path to a new member, who answers questions and reports one confusing step.
2. That step becomes a flag for its owner, and the manager's view shows only the shared completion.

#### KEEP-008 — Stale-knowledge sweeps

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-005, BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-008 · *Rules:* D-1

**Requirement.** Once a week, the knowledge agent prepares each owner one digest of their lapsed verifications, open flags, ownerless pages in their containers and pages nobody has opened in 180 days. Each item comes with a prepared action: re-verify (which opens the revision), accept a fix, reassign, or archive. Its data is status, analytics (`PAGE-013`), flags and ownership. The company policy decides every action: commitment for verification, standard for reversible archive, and access when reassignment changes standing authority. Under the held company policy for commitment, standard and access, the owner performs the prepared actions.

**Acceptance.**
1. a Workers journey advances a week over a seeded workspace and delivers exactly one digest per owner with the expected items.
2. Acting on two items applies the actions and leaves no duplicate notices.

#### KEEP-010 — Team-built agents

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-002, BASE-AGENT-005, BASE-AGENT-006, BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-008 · *Rules:* D-1

**Requirement.** An authorized member builds an agent for their team without code. The agent has a name, instructions, a knowledge scope (containers, labels, cards and connected sources), the tools it may use, and when it runs: Its tools offer search and cited answers (`ANSWER-001`), drafting pages and cards, proposing edits as suggestions (`SUG-001`), filing issues (`EMBED-001`) and posting to a chat channel (`CHAT-001`). Its triggers are asked in Slate, in chat (`CHAT-002`) or over MCP (`API-003`), on a schedule, or on an automation event (`AUTO-*`). Each agent is an `AI-014` agent record. Its builder can test it against sample questions before sharing it with groups. Its data is the intersection of the agent's declared scope and what the member it runs for may read. A scheduled or event run reads as the agent's owner, and its output reaches only an audience that may read every source it used (`AI-013`). Verification carries commitment, publication external, reversible archive standard, permanent deletion destructive and access changes access. The company policy decides execution; under the held company policy for standard or external edits, edits are suggestions and pages stay drafts until the named person accepts them. Every run records its actor, scope, tools, sources and cost against the company’s chosen spend policy (`AI-010`, `AI-012`). Owners can see, pause or delete any agent, and removing an agent's owner pauses it (`WORK-007`).

**Acceptance.**
1. a Workers journey with a provider fake at the network edge builds an agent scoped to one container with the answer and propose-edit tools, and shares it with a group.
2. A group member who can read only half the container asks it a question, and the answer cites only pages that member can read.
3. Under the held company policy for standard or external edits, the agent’s proposed edit lands as a suggestion and changes nothing until the named person accepts it.
4. A page in scope that instructs the agent to publish itself or grant access produces a refusal and no change.
5. A scheduled run posts once to a channel fake, citing only sources its audience can read.
6. Pausing the agent stops its next scheduled run, and exhausting its budget stops it with a notice to its owner.
7. A browser journey at 1440 and 390 builds, tests and shares the agent.

### Agent surface

**Specialist: wiki curator.** It keeps company knowledge organized, cited, current and useful, and follows the inquiry-to-learning loop when the business asks it to investigate.

Inherits BASE-AGENT-001 to BASE-AGENT-013. The company's policy decides every call; Slate presets no disposition.

**How Slate computes each class.**

- **standard.** An internal reversible wiki edit, watch, draft, task or suggestion carries its item count; a move or edit is external as well when it newly exposes content outside the business.
- **external.** A public page, outside share, member or guest invitation, mail retry, chat delivery, audit stream, connector write or externally visible wiki change carries recipient count and counterparty: internal, known from an admitted domain or existing company relationship, new otherwise, or public for an open publication.
- **money.** Paid activation carries the verified amount, currency and counterparty of the charge or changed price.
- **commitment.** An accepted decision, attestation, approval of relied-on content or commercial term carries its value and counterparty; an agent’s act remains distinct from a person’s attestation.
- **accounts.** Creating a paid SSO account or outside resource carries its provider.
- **gated.** A provider’s account consent (including Slack OAuth installation or Teams Entra-admin consent), hosted card entry or identity check carries provider and step when that provider requires a person; an offered agent API uses the company policy for the call’s classes.
- **access.** Membership, groups, guest or page grants, SAML admission allow-lists, restored grants, connector or client authority and governance changes to standing permission carry people affected and widening or narrowing; reassigning a page owner without changing authority remains standard.
- **security.** SSO enforcement, AI-provider, chat or source connector credential custody and changes, token custody, signed-webhook or audit-stream signing and SIEM credentials, audit retention, backup and form anti-spam protective settings carry the affected setting.
- **destructive.** Permanent erasure, connector-content purge, permanent template, saved-conversation, decision-record or saved-view deletion, irreversible field conversion or removal, backup retention deletion or deleting a retained page or attachment version carries the item count; reversible trash, archive and changes recoverable through revision restore remain standard.
- **sensitive.** Reading, writing or exporting source or wiki records containing regulated ID, health, bank, card or payroll data carries record count and data kind; a confidential label alone does not invent this class.
- **live.** A trial effect, operational remediation, learned-procedure activation or skill activation that changes a running service carries that service; a read-only rehearsal remains standard.

## Boundaries

Slate is a US-first owned wiki. These are the jobs it deliberately does not do, and how a buyer gets each one done.

- **Office documents, spreadsheets and slides.** Slate is not a full office suite. Attached Office, OpenDocument and PDF files preview, keep versions and are searchable in Slate (`BLOCK-021`, `BLOCK-022`, `SEARCH-013`), but they are edited in their own applications. Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 files are embedded and linked (`EMBED-003`, `EMBED-004`) and kept in [Chest](https://github.com/just-every/run-chest), Drive or SharePoint, while Slate pages stay the place knowledge is written and co-edited.
- **Whiteboards and diagramming suites.** Slate is not a whiteboard. Figma, Miro and Lucid boards are embedded (`EMBED-003`); diagrams as code (`BLOCK-013`) and diagrams.net diagrams (`BLOCK-019`) are native. Confluence whiteboards are named in the import report with a link to the original (`IMP-010`).
- **Video recording.** Slate does not record video. Loom and YouTube recordings are embedded (`EMBED-003`).
- **Issue tracking, sprints and project portfolios.** These belong to [Vector](https://github.com/just-every/run-vector) or Jira, embedded and connected (`EMBED-001`, `AUTO-007`). Databases can hold a light tracker. Cross-functional project management (Asana, monday.com) stays outside Slate; [Pegboard](https://github.com/just-every/run-pegboard) is the RunEditRun sibling in that category.
- **Chat.** Slack, Microsoft Teams and [Nook](https://github.com/just-every/run-nook) are connected (`CHAT-*`).
- **Large relational databases and internal apps.** These belong to [Cradle](https://github.com/just-every/run-cradle). Slate databases stay within `seed.json → limits`, and beyond them the buyer links a Cradle base.
- **Formal training and compliance certifications.** These belong to [Beam](https://github.com/just-every/run-beam) and [Evidence](https://github.com/just-every/run-evidence). Slate provides reading paths and acknowledgments (`KEEP-007`, `CARD-003`).
- **A customer-facing help center and ticket deflection.** These belong to [HappyToHelp](https://github.com/just-every/run-happytohelp), which can cite Slate pages and cards. Slate publishes pages (`WEB-*`), not a support portal.
- **Identity provider.** Slate is a SAML and OIDC relying party and a SCIM client (`ADMIN-001`, `ADMIN-002`). The directory itself is Okta, Entra ID or [Auth](https://github.com/just-every/run-auth).
- **Freshness and access beyond what a source's API exposes.** Connectors mirror documented ACLs and deletions and show their lag (`CONNECT-002`, `CONNECT-003`). Slate promises nothing beyond what a source's API exposes, and a working credential is never treated as permission to disclose.
- **Hosting frontier models or unbounded compute.** Inference runs at the owner's chosen provider under owner budgets (`ANSWER-006`, `AI-012`). Long jobs run as bounded durable stages within Cloudflare Workers limits.
- **Regulated records management.** Legal hold, records retention schedules, HIPAA and FedRAMP programs are not promised by ordinary wiki security. Buyers keep regulated records in an approved records system and connect scoped knowledge. SOC 2 evidence collection belongs to [Evidence](https://github.com/just-every/run-evidence).
- **Hosting region, currency and language.** Slate is US-first: it is deployed to the buyer's Cloudflare account, budgets are in USD and the interface is in US English. EU data-residency guarantees and localized interfaces are not claimed.
- **Rewriting links stored in other products.** Slate does not edit the Slack or Teams messages, emails, Google Docs or Jira comment text that contain old Confluence URLs, and Confluence does not either when a site moves. Those links still reach the right record through the resolver, chat unfurls, pasted-URL resolution and the browser extension, which IT can force-install on managed browsers (`IMP-013`, `SEARCH-014`, `CARD-002`), and Jira's issue links are re-pointed (`EMBED-006`). Atlassian owns the `atlassian.net` hostname, so after that site is canceled a click on an old link in a browser without the extension reaches Atlassian, not Slate.
- **Native app distribution.** This needs the buyer's or Run Edit Run's Apple and Google developer accounts. That is engineering and release work (`MOBILE-001`, `MOBILE-002`), not a reason to drop the apps.

The words in this contract are the family's, not either product's. A **container** is what Notion calls a teamspace and Confluence a space. A **record** is what Notion calls a page in a database and Confluence an entry. A **page body** is what Notion calls blocks and Confluence elements or macros. A **member** is a person with an account in the workspace; `BASELINE.md` calls the same person an operator, and the two words mean one thing. An edition relabels these words; no clause changes when it does.
- Personal screen-reader and certification receipts, vendor tenants, store approval and elapsed real-world outcomes are field proof; seeded scale, standards providers and official-schema fakes remain acceptance.

**Neighboring products.**

Slate is one product. Where the market sells a neighboring product separately, Slate connects to it and does not rebuild it; when the neighbor is a Run Edit Run sibling, Slate links to that sibling first and to the US incumbent second.

Cross-functional task and project management (Asana, monday.com, ClickUp) stays outside Slate; [Pegboard](https://github.com/just-every/run-pegboard) is the RunEditRun sibling in that category. Slate's databases can hold a lightweight tracker, but Slate does not become a project-management product. Payroll and monitoring/observability also stay outside Slate; [Envelope](https://github.com/just-every/run-envelope) and [Porthole](https://github.com/just-every/run-porthole) are the respective RunEditRun siblings.

The following remain non-goals:

- commercial plan ladders, subscription trials and credits, seat counting and upgrade gates;
- vendor suite chrome;
- a commercial marketplace or storefront;
- coupling to a single issue tracker (Vector and Jira connect through the same embed and automation clauses);
- a bundled screen recorder;
- multiple workspaces per deployment.

Bounded product experiments are not subscription trials. Live co-editing, evaluated formulas and rollups, suggested edits, scoped agent budgets, native apps (`MOBILE-*`), page locks (`PAGE-015`), label filtering (`SEARCH-010`), space blogs (`CONT-010`) and a company hub (`CONT-011`) are in scope.

Some incumbent features are met another way:

- native whiteboards by embeds (`EMBED-003`) and diagrams as code (`BLOCK-013`);
- container calendars by database calendar views (`DB-004`);
- meeting-note specializations by starter templates with assigned tasks (`TMPL-007`, `BLOCK-015`);
- team profiles by the people directory (`WORK-016`).

Contributed tree node kinds beyond pages, databases, cards and posts, and cross-container assignments, remain future extensions; existing page, comment and activity requirements are not waived. The target adds no new policy profile and preserves all eight profiles and every value unchanged. [Boundaries](#boundaries) lists what Slate connects to instead of building.

## Agent access

Every call can carry several risk classes. The server computes them from arguments and current records, and from the provider's answer for gated steps. A seed proposes a new class for the shared list rather than inventing one.

| Class | A call is in it when it… | Measured by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **standard** | stays inside the business and can be undone in the product | items |
| **external** | reaches or exposes anything to someone outside the business | recipients; counterparty *known*, *new* or *public* |
| **money** | moves money or changes what the business pays or charges | amount; counterparty |
| **commitment** (legal) | binds the business: a signature, accepted terms, an offer, a sign-off others rely on | value; counterparty |
| **accounts** | creates an account, identity or paid resource at an outside service | provider |
| **gated** | needs a step that outside services or agent providers commonly keep for a person: a consent screen in someone's account, card entry at a hosted checkout, identity or business verification, terms accepted in a person's name | provider; step |
| **access** | changes standing authority: staff, roles, admins, membership, devices, app and agent grants | people; widens or narrows |
| **security** | changes protective settings, or handles credentials | setting |
| **destructive** | cannot be undone in the product | items |
| **sensitive** | touches regulated personal data: health, ID, bank, card or payroll numbers | records; kind |
| **live** | changes how a running service behaves for its users | service |

Four rules no company policy changes:

1. People set the policy and the Pause switch. An agent may draft a change, and a person confirms it.
2. An agent never widens its own authority: its grant, its sponsor's role, the policy or Pause.
3. An agent acts for a named person, its sponsor, and never beyond that person's role.
4. Attribution is truthful. An agent's act reads `"<agent> for <person>"`, in the record and in the mail and messages it sends outside. It never records a person's approval, confirmation or signature. It never poses as a person to an outside service: no CAPTCHA, and never a person's own password or 2FA code. When a provider insists on a person, that step goes to a person.

Base and the seeds ship no dispositions; each company's policy decides every class.

Policy is data: numbered, signed revisions in the paired Business, adopted within 60 seconds using the installation's existing owner-claim trust; a standalone seed keeps the same document in Agents settings. Setup asks every class in use, each approval rule's approver and wait, and spend caps ("no cap" is an answer), with no answer pre-selected. Within a class, the matching rule with the most scope fields wins; a named class beats `*`, and a tie takes the stricter rule. Across classes the strictest result wins, in order blocked, approval, review, autonomous. Rules can narrow by seed, specialist or agent, threshold per call or per day, counterparty and access direction. These are company choices, never shipped answers.

MCP method names below use spaced slashes; the wire names join those segments without spaces.
